event: Flood begins; fountains of the deep broken up
note: Noah's family and the animals enter the ark the same day (7:13).

event: Ark rests on the mountains of Ararat
note: Exactly five months after the flood began; 7:24 and 8:3 give 150 days.

event: Tops of the mountains seen
note: Waters receded until the tenth month.

event: Waters dried up; Noah removes the ark's covering
note: First day of the new year after the flood.

event: Earth fully dry; Noah told to leave the ark
note: Ten days more than one lunar year after the flood began on 2/17; the command to leave follows in 8:15–16.

event: Passover lambs selected in Egypt
note: The lamb was set apart on the 10th and kept until the 14th (12:6).

event: First Passover; firstborn of Egypt struck at midnight
note: The lamb is killed at evening on the 14th; the plague comes at midnight (12:29), the night of the 14th going into the 15th.

event: Israel departs from Rameses (the Exodus)
note: The day after the Passover; Exodus 12:41 says it fell on the very day the 430 years ended.

event: Arrival in the Wilderness of Sin; manna follows
yearAsWritten: 1st year after the Exodus ("second month after their departing")
note: Quail come that evening and manna the next morning (16:12–14), so manna starts on the 16th by inference.

event: Arrival at the Wilderness of Sinai
note: The text says "the same day" without naming the day; it is often read as the 1st of the month (new moon), and some read it as the 15th.

event: Tabernacle set up
note: The command is in 40:2. Numbers 7:1 and 9:15 describe the same day, with the cloud covering the tabernacle.

event: Passover kept at Sinai
note: First anniversary Passover, kept in the wilderness.

event: Census of Israel ordered at Sinai
note: The congregation assembled on the same day (1:18).

event: Second-month Passover appointed for those who were unclean
note: A ruling given for a specific case that year, and also a standing law; the text does not describe that year's observance, so the owner may skip it.

event: Cloud lifts; Israel sets out from Sinai
Israel at Kadesh in the Desert of Zin; Miriam dies
yearAsWritten: Year not stated (usually taken as the 40th year)
note: Only the month is given; Aaron's death later the same year (33:38) points to the 40th year.

event: Aaron dies on Mount Hor
note: Numbers 20:28 also records his death but gives no date.

event: Moses begins his addresses (Deuteronomy) in Moab
Israel crosses the Jordan and camps at Gilgal
yearAsWritten: Year of entry into Canaan (41st year after the Exodus by inference)
note: The same day of the month the Passover lamb was chosen in Egypt.

event: Passover kept at Gilgal
note: The month comes from 4:19; the verse itself gives only the 14th day.

event: Israel first eats produce of Canaan
note: "The morrow after the passover", read as the 15th.

event: Manna ceases
note: Worked out from the text: the day after they first ate the land's produce.

event: New-moon feast; David's seat empty two days
note: The month is not named. The feast is on the new moon (day 1, 20:24) and David is missed again on day 2.

event: Gadites cross the flooded Jordan to join David
yearAsWritten: While David was at Ziklag/the stronghold (no year)
note: Month only.

event: Solomon begins building the Temple
yearAsWritten: 4th year of Solomon's reign; 480th year after the Exodus (1 Kings 6:1)
note: 1 Kings 6:1 and 6:37 give only the month (Zif = 2nd). The day comes from 2 Chronicles 3:2, where some scholars think "second day" may be a copying slip.

event: Temple completed
note: Month Bul (8th), no day given.

event: Temple dedication assembly at the feast of the seventh month
yearAsWritten: Year not stated (after the Temple was finished)
note: Month Ethanim (7th). The feast is Tabernacles (normally from day 15), held after a seven-day altar dedication (2 Chronicles 7:9).

event: People sent home after the Temple dedication
note: 1 Kings 8:66 says "on the eighth day" and 8:65 says fourteen days of feasting. Chronicles gives the 23rd, the day after the eighth-day assembly.

event: Jeroboam's rival feast at Bethel
note: This feast is set one month after Judah's feast of the 7th month.

event: Asa's covenant assembly in Jerusalem
note: Month only.

event: Hezekiah begins cleansing the Temple
note: 29:3 says he opened the Temple doors in the first month of his first year.

event: Cleansing reaches the porch of the Temple
Temple cleansing completed
note: Completed too late for the normal 1/14 Passover, so it was moved to the second month (30:2–3).

event: Hezekiah's Passover in the second month
note: Seven days of Unleavened Bread followed (30:21), and the people extended it by seven more days (30:23).

event: Tithe heaps begun
note: Month only.

event: Tithe heaps completed
note: Month only.

event: Josiah's Passover
note: 2 Kings 23:21–23 describes the same Passover and gives the year but not the day.

event: Nebuchadnezzar begins the siege of Jerusalem
note: Jeremiah 52:4 and Ezekiel 24:1 agree on 10/10; Jeremiah 39:1 gives only the month.

event: Famine in the city; wall breached; Zedekiah flees
note: In the KJV 2 Kings 25:3, "fourth month" is in italics, meaning the translators added it from Jeremiah 52:6; Jeremiah 39:2 also states it.

event: Nebuzaradan comes to Jerusalem (2 Kings reckoning)
note: Disagrees with Jeremiah 52:12, which gives the 10th. The two are often reconciled as arrival on the 7th and burning on the 10th.

event: Nebuzaradan enters Jerusalem; Temple burned (Jeremiah reckoning)
note: The parallel 2 Kings 25:8 gives the 7th day.

event: Gedaliah assassinated at Mizpah
note: Month only; Jeremiah 41:1 likewise gives only the month.

event: Evil-merodach releases Jehoiachin (2 Kings reckoning)
yearAsWritten: 37th year of Jehoiachin's captivity; Evil-merodach's accession year
note: Disagrees with Jeremiah 52:31, which gives the 25th.

event: Evil-merodach releases Jehoiachin (Jeremiah reckoning)
yearAsWritten: 37th year of Jehoiachin's captivity; first year of Evil-merodach
note: The parallel 2 Kings 25:27 gives the 27th.

event: Hananiah's false prophecy in the Temple
yearAsWritten: 4th year of Zedekiah ("beginning of the reign")
note: Month only.

event: Hananiah dies
note: Month only; two months after his prophecy.

event: Fast proclaimed; Baruch reads Jeremiah's scroll
note: Month only.

event: Jehoiakim burns the scroll in his winter house
note: Month only, and the same month as 36:9. It may be the same day or soon after.

event: Returned exiles resume burnt offerings on the altar
yearAsWritten: 1st year of the return under Cyrus (implied)
note: The people gathered as the seventh month arrived (3:1).

event: Returned exiles keep the Feast of Tabernacles
note: The feast is named but no day is given; 15 is the feast's set day.

event: Work on the second Temple foundation begins
yearAsWritten: 2nd year of their coming to Jerusalem
note: Month only.

event: Second Temple completed
note: Month Adar. The apocryphal 1 Esdras 7:5 gives the 23rd of Adar.

event: Passover after the Temple's completion
yearAsWritten: 7th year of Darius by inference (the month after Adar of year 6)
note: Unleavened Bread followed for seven days (6:22).

event: Ezra begins the journey up from Babylon
note: 8:31 gives the departure from the Ahava river as 1/12. The 1st is the start of the journey and the 12th the actual setting out.

event: Ezra's company departs from the river Ahava
note: See Ezra 7:9.

event: Ezra arrives in Jerusalem
note: 7:8 gives only the month.

event: Assembly in the rain over foreign marriages
yearAsWritten: Year not stated (presumably the 7th of Artaxerxes)

event: Inquiry into foreign marriages begins
Inquiry into foreign marriages completed
Nehemiah hears of Jerusalem's ruin in Shushan
note: Month Chisleu (9th), no day given.

event: Nehemiah's request to Artaxerxes
note: Month Nisan, no day given. Both 1:1 and 2:1 are in the 20th year, which suggests a regnal year that does not begin in Nisan.

event: Jerusalem's wall completed in 52 days
note: Month Elul (6th).

event: Ezra reads the Law to the assembly
yearAsWritten: Year of the wall's completion (implied by 7:73)

event: Leaders gather to study the Law; booths commandment found
note: "On the second day" of the month.

event: Feast of Booths kept
note: The feast is named but no start day is given; 15 is the feast's set day. Ezra read from the Law on each of the seven days (8:18).

event: Solemn assembly on the eighth day of the feast
note: Day worked out as the eighth day from 7/15.

event: Fast and confession of sins
note: "This month" refers back to the 7th month.

event: Esther taken to King Ahasuerus
note: Month Tebeth, no day given.

event: Pur (the lot) cast before Haman
note: Month Nisan; the lot fell on the 12th month, Adar.

event: Haman's decree written and sealed
note: The decree set the attack for 12/13 (3:13).

event: Mordecai's counter-decree written
note: Month Sivan.

event: Day appointed for the attack; the Jews prevail
note: Month Adar. The date was set by both decrees (3:13, 8:12).

event: Second day of fighting in Shushan
Jews of the provinces rest and feast
note: Unwalled villages kept the 14th (9:19).

event: Jews of Shushan rest and feast
Purim established as a yearly feast (14th and 15th of Adar)
note: Mordecai's letter (9:20) is not dated. The feast covers 12/14–15, and the queen confirms it in 9:29–32.

event: Ezekiel's opening vision by the Chebar
note: What the "thirtieth year" counts from is unclear; it is often taken as Ezekiel's age.

event: Vision of abominations in the Temple
note: The Greek Septuagint reads the fifth month.

event: Elders come to inquire of the LORD
Word that Babylon has begun the siege
note: Same day as the siege's start in 2 Kings 25:1 and Jeremiah 52:4.

event: Oracle against Tyre
note: No month is named; only "the first day of the month" is given.

event: Oracle against Pharaoh and Egypt
Egypt given to Nebuchadnezzar as wages
note: The latest dated oracle in Ezekiel.

event: Pharaoh's arm broken
Pharaoh compared to the fallen cedar
Lament over Pharaoh
note: Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac read the 11th year.

event: Lament over Egypt's descent to the pit
note: No month is named in the Hebrew. It is usually taken as the 12th month (as in 32:1); the Septuagint reads the first month.

event: Fugitive reports that Jerusalem has fallen
note: Some Hebrew manuscripts, the Septuagint and the Syriac read the 11th year.

event: Vision of the future Temple
yearAsWritten: 25th year of our captivity; 14th year after the city was struck
note: The text says "beginning of the year", not a numbered month. It is usually read as month 1. Some read it as the 7th month, where the 10th is the Day of Atonement and the start of a Jubilee year.

event: Daniel's vision by the Tigris (Hiddekel)
yearAsWritten: 3rd year of Cyrus king of Persia (10:1)
note: Follows three weeks of mourning (10:2–3).

event: Haggai's first message: rebuild the house
Work on the Temple resumes
Haggai's message on the latter glory of the house
note: The last day of the Feast of Tabernacles (7/15–21).

event: Haggai's message on defilement and blessing
note: 2:18 links this day to the laying of the Temple foundation.

event: Haggai's second message the same day, to Zerubbabel
note: The verse gives only "the 24th day of the month"; the month comes from 2:10.

event: Zechariah's first call to return
note: Month only.

event: Zechariah's night visions begin
note: Month Sebat.

event: Question from Bethel about the fasts
note: Month Chisleu. The fasts mentioned (7:3, 7:5, 8:19) are yearly observances in months 4, 5, 7 and 10, not separate events.

event: Jesus at age twelve in the Temple at Passover
note: The feast is named but no day is given. He stayed behind after "the days" of the feast were fulfilled (2:43).

event: Passover visit; Jesus cleanses the Temple
yearAsWritten: First Passover of the ministry in John
note: Signs are done "at the passover, in the feast day" (2:23). The day is the feast's set day, not given in the text.

event: Feeding of the five thousand, with Passover near
note: The text says Passover was "nigh", so the event comes shortly before 1/14.

event: Feast of Tabernacles at hand; Jesus goes up secretly
note: The feast is named but no day is given. 7:14 has him teaching "about the midst of the feast", which by inference is about 7/18.

event: "Last day, that great day of the feast"
note: The day is ambiguous: 7/21 (seventh day) or 7/22 (eighth-day assembly).

event: Jesus at the Feast of Dedication
note: The feast is not in the Hebrew Bible. Its date (25 Chislev) comes from 1 Maccabees 4:52–59.

event: Jesus comes to Bethany six days before Passover; anointed by Mary
note: Worked out as six days before 1/14; it could be the 8th or 9th depending on how the days are counted. The triumphal entry is "the next day" (12:12).

event: "After two days is the passover": the plot to kill Jesus
note: Worked out from "after two days"; it could be the 12th or 13th.

event: Last Supper prepared on the "first day of unleavened bread"
note: The Synoptics put the meal on the evening the lamb was killed (Mark 14:12, Luke 22:7). John (13:1, 18:28, 19:14) puts the meal before Passover, which conflicts.

event: Crucifixion on the preparation of the Passover
note: John puts the death on 1/14 and calls the next day a "high" sabbath (19:31). The Synoptic timeline implies 1/15.

event: Holy Spirit given on the day of Pentecost
note: Pentecost falls in the 3rd month, 50 days after the wave-sheaf. Which day depends on the calendar (the DSS calendar gives 3/15; the rabbinic calendar 3/6), so the day is left for the engine.

event: Herod arrests Peter during the days of Unleavened Bread
yearAsWritten: Year of Herod Agrippa I's persecution
note: Sometime between 1/15 and 1/21. Herod intended to bring Peter out after the Passover (12:4; KJV "Easter").

event: Paul sails from Philippi after Unleavened Bread
note: After 1/21; he reaches Troas five days later.

event: Paul hurries to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost
note: An intention rather than a dated arrival; he arrives in 21:17 with no date given.

event: Paul's warning after "the fast" had passed
note: "The fast" is the Day of Atonement (7/10); the warning comes after it.
